summary: Nearly all visitors need a Ugandan visa, applied for online through the official eVisa portal (USD 50 single entry) before travel; East African Community citizens move freely, and a list of mostly African, Caribbean and Commonwealth countries is visa-exempt. A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required from every traveler.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: Uganda requires a yellow fever vaccination certificate (ICVP) from all travelers aged 1 year and over, regardless of where you arrive from. The eVisa application asks you to upload it, and it is checked again on arrival.

source.name: Uganda Electronic Visa/Permit Application System — Directorate of Citizenship and Immigration Control

vaccinations.name: Malaria prophylaxis
vaccinations.text: Malaria is present year-round throughout Uganda, including Kampala. Antimalarial tablets, repellent and bed nets are strongly recommended — talk to a travel clinic before your trip.

source.name: Uganda Electronic Visa/Permit Application System — Directorate of Citizenship and Immigration Control

travelInsurance.text: Not required for entry, but comprehensive medical coverage is strongly recommended — good hospitals are limited outside Kampala and evacuation coverage matters for trekking itineraries.

source.name: Uganda Electronic Visa/Permit Application System — Directorate of Citizenship and Immigration Control

onwardTicket.text: Immigration may ask for a return or onward ticket and evidence of accommodation, though checks are not systematic for tourists.

proofOfFunds.text: No fixed amount is published; be ready to show means of support for your stay if asked.

notes: Uganda bans single-use plastic carrier bags — pack without them.
Drones require prior clearance from the Civil Aviation Authority and security ministries — arrange permits well before travel.

payments.text: Cards work at upmarket Kampala hotels, malls and safari lodges, but everyday Uganda runs on cash and mobile money (MTN MoMo, Airtel Money). Carry shillings, plus clean US dollar notes printed 2013 or later for lodges and permits.

safety.text: Most visits, including gorilla trekking in Bwindi, are trouble-free. Petty crime occurs in Kampala, and pockets of insecurity persist near the DRC border and in remote parts of Karamoja. Take local advice for border areas. Uganda also has severe laws criminalising same-sex relations, which LGBTQ+ travelers should weigh before visiting.

source.name: U.S. Department of State — Uganda Travel Advisory

bestTimeToVisit.text: The two dry seasons — December to February and June to August — are best for gorilla trekking and savannah safaris; rains peak around March–May and October–November, when forest trails get slippery.

idp.text: Uganda is a party to both the 1949 Geneva and the 1968 Vienna Conventions on Road Traffic, so it recognizes an International Driving Permit issued under either.

driving.text: Uganda is a party to both the 1949 Geneva and the 1968 Vienna Conventions on Road Traffic, so it recognizes an International Driving Permit issued under either. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for Uganda yet.

tips.text: Uganda checks yellow fever certificates from every traveler, whatever your route — get vaccinated at least 10 days before travel and carry the ICVP card with your passport.
Combining Uganda with Kenya and Rwanda? The USD 100 East Africa Tourist Visa covers all three countries for 90 days with multiple entries between them. Apply through the country you enter first.
Uganda has no visa on arrival for most nationalities. Apply at visas.immigration.go.ug before flying and travel with the printed approval letter; avoid unofficial visa websites.
Gorilla-trekking permits (about USD 800 in Bwindi) are strictly limited and sell out months ahead. Book through the Uganda Wildlife Authority or a licensed operator well in advance.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Uganda?
faq.answer: Most visitors do — Uganda uses an eVisa system, with the single-entry tourist visa at USD 50 applied for online before travel. East African Community citizens enter freely, and nationals of a list of mostly African, Caribbean and Commonwealth countries are visa-exempt.

faq.question: Can I get a visa on arrival in Uganda?
faq.answer: Uganda has moved visa issuance online. You should apply at visas.immigration.go.ug before travel and carry the approval letter, which is exchanged for the visa on arrival. Airlines generally will not board visa-required passengers without the approval.

faq.question: What is the East Africa Tourist Visa?
faq.answer: A joint USD 100 visa covering Uganda, Kenya and Rwanda for 90 days, with multiple entries between the three countries. Apply through the country you enter first — if that is Uganda, via the official Ugandan eVisa portal.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever certificate for Uganda?
faq.answer: Yes — unlike most countries, Uganda requires the certificate from all travelers aged 1 year and over regardless of departure point. You upload it with the eVisa application and show it on arrival.

faq.question: How long does the Uganda eVisa take?
faq.answer: Approvals usually come through in 2–7 business days, but allow at least two weeks in case additional documents are requested. You will need a passport scan, photo, yellow fever certificate and travel details.
